requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase. The skill MUST direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example, identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement, and report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review.
rationale:
The reviewed test adequately checks `requirements.cli.bootstrap_skill`.

**Test reviewed.** It is `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bootstrap_skill_is_bundled_and_directs_complete_inventories]`, which carries the `{test}` reference. Its helpers `bundled_skill`, `assert_phrases`, `assert_text`, `assert_in_order` and `assert_text_in_order` are reached from it. They read the real `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md` through `skill_files`, which uses `include_str!`. They collapse whitespace, so phrases that span line breaks in the file still match. They fail with a message when a phrase is missing or out of order.

**Obligations and their assertions.** The requirement is about what a bundled skill must direct, so checking the skill's text for the directing phrases is the appropriate verification.

| Obligation | Assertions | Where the skill text sits |
|---|---|---|
| Habeas bundles the skill | `SKILLS` contains the name. The description starts with "Use when adopting Habeas in an existing codebase". The skill's text comes from `include_str!` of the asset file, so it cannot compile without that file. | Front matter of `SKILL.md`. |
| Direct agents to read the code and tests | The phrases "Read the existing requirements, documentation, public entry points, implementation, and tests" and "Follow behavior through the code". | Workflow step 2. |
| Map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example | The phrases "every first-party runnable test or test case", "Record the behavior each test checks; fill in requirement names…" and "Every test must end up with a `{test}` reference to a requirement or example". | Inventories and Tagging sections. |
| Identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality | The phrases "every function, method, struct, enum, and union, listed from the source…", "public APIs, commands, handlers, UI actions, configuration, outputs, errors, and distinct observable branches", "A tagged entry point doesn't mean every observable branch beneath it has a requirement" and "Give every inventoried test and each requirement's roots their references". | Inventories and Tagging sections. |
| Report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review | An ordered check of four phrases: the recount "without your lists" (workflow step 8), the gap-list line format, "Claim 100% only when both inventories have no unmapped items", and "Don't silently exclude difficult cases". The order matches the skill, where the recount comes before the report. | Workflow step 8 and the Report section. |

**Other tests.** `the_bootstrap_skill_is_home_of_deriving_an_initial_requirement_set` and the `home_markers` checks add structural coverage of the same skill. They are not needed for adequacy.

**Gaps.** I found none. No obligation in the requirement text is left unasserted, and no `{fixme}` acknowledgments apply. Phrase-presence assertions are weaker than a behavioral check. Here, though, the obligation is only that the skill text directs agents, so the assertions match what the requirement asks for.
